claim_text: The process of nitriding [of steels] is conducted at temperatures 500-570°C in an ammonia atmosphere.

caveats.text: The 500-570°C range is standard for gas nitriding specifically. Other nitriding methods (plasma, salt bath) operate at different temperature ranges and atmospheres.
Some authoritative sources give a narrower range of 495-565°C (Neal Systems) or 500-530°C (ScienceDirect), while others extend the upper limit to 580-650°C.
At temperatures above ~560-570°C, the compound layer can become porous due to increased ammonia dissociation.
The claim implicitly refers to gas nitriding. Plasma nitriding can operate from 340-590°C, and salt bath nitriding typically at ~570°C using molten cyanide salts rather than ammonia.

claim_text: Нитриды молибдена обеспечивают дисперсионное твердение [в контексте процесса азотирования]

caveats.text: Mo is a weak nitride former (Group 2 in Лахтин classification) — its nitrides form only via solid-state reaction.
Mo nitride precipitation is kinetically delayed due to large volume misfit with the ferrite matrix.
The dispersion hardening contribution of Mo₂N (γ=0.4) is lower than CrN (γ=1.2), VN (γ=0.8), TiN (γ=2.0).
